deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a handwritten English excerpt headed 'pag. 1.' The text closely matches the opening of Sir David Brewster's 'Memoirs of the Life, Writings, and Discoveries of Sir Isaac Newton' (1855), Vol. I, ch. 1; I am recalling this match rather than checking it against the book.

Content:
(i) Laplace, 'to whom posterity will probably assign the place next to Newton', called the Principia pre-eminent above all productions of human intellect. This, the excerpt says, removes any extravagance from Halley's contemporary praise of Newton.
(ii) Halley's verse from his ode prefixed to the Principia is quoted: 'Nec fas est propius mortali attingere Divos'. Its English rendering is 'So near the gods — man cannot nearer go.'
(iii) Biographical facts follow:
- Newton was born at Woolsthorpe, a hamlet in Colsterworth parish, Lincolnshire, about six miles south of Grantham, on 25 December 1642 Old Style.
- This is said to be 'exactly one year after Galileo died'.
- He was baptized at Colsterworth on 1 January 1642/3. The double year reflects Old Style dating, in which the legal year began on 25 March.
- His father, Isaac Newton senior, died aged thirty-six, 'a little more than a year after the death of his ...'. The text breaks off here.

The ellipses at start and end mark this as a fragment copied from a printed source. The upper-right note 'Riemann 18' and the circled folio number '36' are later archival markings. The hand, an English cursive with Germanic letter forms, may be Riemann's or another copyist's. Either way, it is an English reading or copying exercise, or excerpting from Brewster, not original work. There are no derivations to reconstruct.
errors: The claim 'exactly one year after Galileo died' is loose. Galileo died on 8 January 1642 in the Gregorian calendar, which Italy used. Newton's birth on 25 December 1642 Old Style is 4 January 1643 Gregorian. Within a single calendar the gap is about 361 days, not exactly one year. The coincidence only appears when the two calendars are mixed; the error belongs to the source text, not the copyist.
No mathematical errors, since there is no mathematics on the page.
